question.text: The normal at $\left(2, \frac{3}{2}\right)$ to the ellipse, $\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{3}=1$ touches a parabola, whose equation is

solution.text:
Ellipse is $\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{3}=1$
Now, equation of normal at $(2,3 / 2)$ is
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{16 x}{2}-\frac{3 y}{3 / 2}=16-3 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 8 x-2 y=13 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad y=4 x-\frac{13}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$
Let $y=4 x-\frac{13}{2}$ touches a parabola $y^2=4 a x$.
We know, a straight line $y=m x+c$ touches a parabola $y^2=4 a x$ if $a-m c=0$
$$
\therefore \quad a-(4)\left(-\frac{13}{2}\right)=0 \Rightarrow a=-26
$$
Hence, required equation of parabola is $y^2=4(-26) x=-104 x$
